title: Sasai: He made the world
hookLine: a chair on a carpenter's bench: the Patti's first letter says the world was made, and its Maker is the one Master of all

cards: Sawdust on the floor, a half-built chair on the bench, and a carpenter running a thumb along a joint to feel whether it sits true. Nobody in that workshop would say the chair just happened.

It's being made: measured, cut, fitted, on purpose. The Patti, the alphabet poem we opened yesterday, starts with a maker's word like that, and uses it for the whole world. Its first letter is sasai, the letter S.

teach.h: SAAJEE: FASHIONED, LIKE A POTTER'S WORK.
teach.b: Here's the first stanza, in paraphrase: S.
The One who fashioned the world is the one Master of all.

teach.h: SERVICE MAKES A LIFE BEAR FRUIT.
teach.b: Those whose minds stay fixed in that One's service, their coming into the world bears fruit. First, the word for made: saajee, fashioned, shaped, put together, the way a carpenter or a potter makes.
The world, in this first letter, isn't an accident lying around. It's been put together on purpose. Second, one Master of all.
Sabhnaa, of all of them. Not a master for the rich and another for the poor, not one for this village and another for the next.
Some readers draw a quiet claim from that: if the same hand made everyone, nobody belongs to a different owner. Third, look what the stanza does next. It doesn't stop at admiring creation.

It turns to the person reading: those who serve with their minds attached, their coming is safal, bearing fruit. The question shifts from who made the world to what you'll do in it. Fourth, why start here.
A school slate could begin with anything.

teach.h: EVERY LETTER READ IN THIS LIGHT.
teach.b: Guru Nanak's begins with the Maker, before anything else is learned, and every letter after is read in that light.
The coffee cup, the sidewalk, the person in line ahead of you all fall under the same first letter.

how: Sikhs speak of God as Karta Purakh, the Creator, and the Patti, sung in Raga Asa, opens with that thought on its first letter; the idea that one Creator made everyone is taught as a basis for equality and seva.

o: a greeting said when entering a gurdwara
the sound sung at the end of a prayer
the letter S, opening with the Maker of all

p: the letter S, the Patti's first
of all: one Master for everyone

s: the Patti's first stanza is only about creation
it turns at once to the reader: those who serve, their coming bears fruit.

games.q: you're writing the first line of an alphabet for a child's slate. what goes on it?
o: the One who made the world, Master of all.
a rule for sitting still in class.
games.why: Guru Nanak's Patti opens with sasai: the One who fashioned the world is the one Master of all, and serving makes a life bear fruit.

practice: Let your eyes rest on one thing near you, a plant, your own hand, the sky through a window, and look at it as if it had been shaped on purpose: its edges, its color, how it holds together.

Then look at the next thing the same way, with no need to explain anything. If you pray, say Waheguru, wonderful Lord, as you look; if not, let each thing be something someone could have made with care.

wordCard.voice: Sasai. The letter S, the Patti's first letter: the One who fashioned the world is the one Master of all, and serving that One makes a life bear fruit. Today's word.

orig.note: sasai: by the letter S; the word that opens the first stanza of Guru Nanak's Patti.

carryVoice: Your line: he made it. The week ran from a pandit's reading to a riverbank, deeds written down, the Oankar closed and the Patti opened. Week done.

sources.ref: Asa, Mahala 1, Patti, stanza 1 ('sasai soe srisat jin saajee sabhnaa saahib ek bhaiaa'), Ang 432
